requirement:
After a rejection under {cite}`requirements.authoring.line_numbers.rejection`,
a submission whose `rationale` is exactly the UUID that rejection gave MUST
accept the rejected submission unchanged, ignoring the new submission's other
fields. Any other rationale that cites line numbers MUST fail the assessment, so
an assessment rejects at most one submission. The UUID MUST NOT be recorded in
evidence.
rationale:
I found no gap against `requirements.authoring.line_numbers.resubmission`. Each obligation has code that carries it out and a test that runs that code.

**Obligations and code**
- **Exact-UUID rationale accepts the rejected submission unchanged, ignoring other fields.**
  - `src/authoring/line_numbers.rs#impl[Rejection]/fn[resubmitted]` returns a clone of the stored rejected arguments only when `rationale(arguments)` equals the stored UUID exactly. The comparison reads only the rationale, so other fields are ignored.
  - `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[converse]` calls `resubmitted` before `decide`. It parses the rejected value and returns that result, so the rejected submission is what gets accepted.
- **Any other rationale citing line numbers fails the assessment, so at most one submission is rejected.** In `src/authoring/line_numbers.rs#impl[Rejection]/fn[decide]`, a citing rationale with `self.rejected` already set returns `Outcome::Fail`. `converse` turns that into an error. A first citation is rejected and stored, so only one rejection can occur.
- **The UUID is not recorded in evidence.** The UUID appears only in the tool-result message and in `Rejection`'s private state. The evidence comes from parsing either the rejected arguments or a clean resubmission, neither of which holds the UUID.

**Tests**
- `src/authoring/line_numbers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_rejection_gives_a_uuid_that_keeps_the_rejected_submission]` carries a `{test}` reference to the subject. It covers these cases:
  - The exact UUID returns the rejected submission even though the `determination` field differs.
  - A UUID with a trailing space returns `None`.
  - A clean resubmission is accepted.
  - A citing rationale after a rejection returns `Fail`.
  - A new `Rejection` gives a different UUID.
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_rationale_citing_line_numbers_is_rejected_once]` carries a `{test}` reference to the subject and runs the whole conversation through `converse` with three follow-ups:
  - The exact UUID is accepted with the original rationale, and the UUID does not appear in the evidence.
  - A clean rationale replaces the rejected one.
  - A rationale citing line numbers again fails with the "after a rejection" error.

`converse` and `decide` carry the `{impl}` references. `resubmitted` is reachable from `converse`, so it needs none of its own. I found no unspecified extra behavior in the code that carries out this requirement.

When the only submission in a response under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.submission`, or a `submit_verification` call under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.verifier_prompt`, is otherwise valid but its
rationale cites line numbers under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.line_numbers.detection`, and it is the
assessment's first such submission, the harness MUST reject it instead of
accepting it and continue the conversation. The tool result MUST quote the
matched text, repeat the location guidance of
{cite}`requirements.authoring.judgment_rules`, and give a fresh random UUID,
saying the model may submit once more, either without line numbers or with
`rationale` set to exactly that UUID to keep the rejected submission as it was.
A rejection MUST be counted in usage like any other turn.
